# ->DEDICATION<- #

...[benefit,] carried a special heroic affection, desire, love, and favor for it; indeed, they even occupied themselves with it at times, finding delight and refreshment in it. (For it is an exceedingly lovely and remarkably pleasant Study, so that one who catches even a single glimpse **through the cracks of the gates** <note>original Latin: *per portarum rimas*</note> into this philosophical **Secret Garden of the Hesperides** <note>In Greek mythology, the Hesperides were nymphs who guarded a garden of golden apples; in alchemical literature, this is a common metaphor for the hidden path to creating "philosophical gold."</note>, as a lover of the art, can never again let it go.) Furthermore, Your Imperial Majesty follows this highly praiseworthy example of your ancestors with great fame and praise, sparing no expense to learn something therein and to reach a blessed end. Indeed, so that such **Chemical Works** <note>original: *Chemische Opera*</note> and writings may not be suppressed, but rather may come to light for the use of many, you have shown and proven all kinds of most gracious promotion through **Special Imperial Privileges** <note>These were legal protections or licenses granted by the Emperor, similar to a modern copyright or patent, allowing the author the sole right to publish the work.</note>.

Thus, I have wished to bring together into a small manual and publish for the benefit of the **sons of doctrine** <note>original Latin: *Filiis doctrinæ*; a traditional term for students or initiates of the alchemical mysteries.</note> in this form, this little work by three highly enlightened, precious, highly experienced, and excellent men and Philosophers, which I have titled **THE GOLDEN TRIPLE LITTLE TREASURY** <note>original Latin: *THESAVRINELLAM AVREAM TRIPARTITAM*</note>. I have divided it into three separate little treatises because they are of **the same tone** <note>original Latin: *eiusdem tenoris*</note> and content, and they deal with the **miracle of the chemical Stone of Nature** <note>original Latin: *Chemico lapidis Physici miraculo*; referring to the Philosopher's Stone.</note> which they left behind in their writings.

The first little treatise is by our highly precious monarch and Philosopher, **Philippus Theophrastus Paracelsus** (who flourished with his Philosophy and Wonder-Medicine from the year 1530 and thereafter until 1541, and in that same year on September 24th, passed away blessedly in Christ). ### TETRAGRAMMATON.
<note>"Tetragrammaton" refers to the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, often used in mystical contexts to represent the divine essence.</note>

<margin>Description of the Trinity.</margin>
From eternity, God was, and the second person of the Godhead is born from eternity from the Father: and from both of them, from eternity, proceeds the third person, the Spirit of God; all three of equal power in one single divine, inseparable essence: through whom all things were created and preserved. When the highest Trinity of God resolved in the divine, most wise counsel to create the world, the angels, mankind, and in short <note>original: "in Summa"</note> all of nature, then God the Father, through the Word as the second person, created things not into their final essence, but only into the **confused prime matter** <note>original: "primam materiam confusam." In alchemy, this is the "First Matter," a chaotic, undifferentiated substance containing the potential for all things.</note>, that is, the **Matrix** <note>original: "Matricem"</note>, in which all creatures of the whole world were mixed together: for which reason it was then called by the philosophers and in Holy Scripture the **Abyss of the Earth** <note>original: "Abusa terra vel Abyssus terræ"</note>; likewise, a thing in which all things lie hidden.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Adam’s creation. [God] created [him]; and not from common red clay, as many wish to insist upon according to the literal word.

One might, however, reproach me here and say: it is not untrue that the human body is the most magnificent substance among all other creatures; nonetheless, it was at first only common clay, and it would have been possible for God to create a magnificent body out of humble earth, since he created the entire world out of nothing. To this I answer: Because of God’s omnipotence, I must confess that it would certainly have been possible for God to create a magnificent body out of common earth. However, because God created all things—in short, the whole of nature—according to the wisest **philosophical order** <note>The author argues that God works through the laws of nature and "spiritual chemistry" rather than through random, chaotic miracles.</note>, and not confusedly against the order of nature; and as He still daily maintains nature in its right order and acts as a creator and multiplier through it until the end of the world—acting *according* to nature and not *against* nature—it is at least probable that in the creation of man or his **Body** <note>original: "Corporis"</note>, God did not act against nature by making that noble body out of the coarsest element of the earth.

I grant that the form and appearance of the matter of the **Limbus** <note>The "Limbus" is an alchemical term for the "edge" or "border" matter—the refined extract of all elements used to build the human form.</note> looked like an earth; but for all that, it was not common earth. Instead, the most subtle essence of the entire **Cosmic Machine** <note>original: "Machinæ mundi"</note> was brought together into one **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, which looked similar to the soil of the earth.

<margin>
Earth is a mother of all elements; therefore, she can be impregnated by all the others.
</margin>

For the earth is a mother of all elements; therefore she can be impregnated by all the others. It follows necessarily from this that her birth was then the **Microcosm** <note>original: "Microcosmus," the "little world" or man as a reflection of the universe.</note>, or a new little world that went forth, as a **Practical Philosopher** <note>original: "Philosophus practicalis," likely referring to an alchemist or natural philosopher who learns through experiment.</note> proves when he says: **Earth is the mother of the elements, which proceed from the earth and return to the earth.** <note>original Latin: "Terra est mater elementorum, quę de terra procedunt, & ad terram reuertuntur."</note> Also: **After separation and impregnation, it shall ascend into heaven and return to its earth, and shall possess the power of both higher and lower things.** <note>original Latin: "Post separationem & imprægnationem ascendet in cœlum, & reuertetur in terram suam, & habebit vim superiorum & inferiorum." This is a famous passage from the *Emerald Tablet*, a foundational text of alchemy.</note> 

In short, God created all things according to the right order of nature and nothing against nature, with the exception of the **First Matter** <note>original: "Prima M." or Prima Materia, the chaotic, formless substance that existed before the world was shaped.</note> from which everything was thereafter created. That same matter was made out of nothing, which is why it is also called the **Abyss** <note>original: "Abyssus"</note>, that is, the **Womb of the World** <note>original: "Matrix mundi"</note>, or the Water from which everything was subsequently created; that same substance was created or made out of nothing.

If God had wished to create something against nature from this material—or the Water over which the Spirit of God hovered—He would not have required six days to do so, nor would He have separated one thing after another according to the precise order of nature. Instead, He could easily have created all creatures in a single moment outside of the Water. But God did not want to make spirits, but rather natural creatures. Therefore, He first took the "casing" <note>The "Kasten" or box refers to the physical frame or container of the material world.</note> before Him...

Therefore, let no one venture to see Paradise, let alone find the place entirely or eat from the fruits of eternal life, without the aforementioned equipment. It has already been mentioned how **ADAM**, our physical father, so terribly lost the great grace of **God** and Divine Wisdom through disobedience and pride. Now, **ADAM** together with his children would have had to remain in this curse forever. Thus, **God** took pity on the repentant man because of His image, the noble soul, and first cursed the serpent as the instrument of the Fall, decreeing that it must go upon its belly and eat the earth. And since the golden heaven may not be opened by anything impure, much less may His golden Son enter into an impure, stained body: so He must instead unite Himself with a metallic body of the female sex, if He intends to redeem the metals. Into this, the golden heaven—the golden little book in which the Father, Son, and Spirit (that is, **SALT**, **SULFUR**, and **Mercury**) lie locked—must be thrown, and then it disappears within. # Of the well-born, highly experienced and excellent Philosopher, Lord Bernard, Count of the March and Treviso, etc. <note>original: "Bernhardi, Graffen von der Marck vnd Teruis." Bernard of Treviso (1406–1490) was a legendary Italian alchemist often cited in Hermetic literature.</note>

## THE APOSTLES’ CREED <note>original: "SYMBOLVM APOSTOLICVM"</note> explained Cabalistically, yet simply, and compared with the great ancient Philosopher’s Stone.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'I' featuring ornate foliate and scrollwork patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>
In this following teaching you will find the knowledge of God of the Holy Trinity, the knowledge of the Holy Angels; you also will find the wealth of your souls and health of body.

**I believe in God)** We should place all our comfort, hope, and confidence solely in the naked grace of God and His mercy, that the same alone—and no creature, let it be as holy as it may—can help us in all our anxiety and need.

**The Father)** And because He is also our Father, we believe firmly that He wishes to help us from the heart, and to stand by us in all our need, and nevermore forsake us, neither here nor there.

**Almighty)** Because He is almighty God, we believe that He can protect and preserve us from everything that is against us: for He is strong enough for all our enemies through His omnipotence.

**A Creator of Heaven and Earth)** So we believe that He has all His creatures in His hand, so that they can do us no single harm without His fatherly will. Therefore, we expect all goods and also eternal life from this Almighty LORD and Creator alone, for all things come from Him alone and can be given by Him. For He wishes to give Himself entirely, with all that He is and has, with heaven and earth along with all creatures, to us, so that they must serve us and be useful, and further us toward eternal life.

Now concerning the earthly power <term>earthly power: here referring to the "virtue" or latent energy within physical matter</term>, which comes from God and was made through His Word: In the beginning God the LORD created heaven and earth, and the earth was void, and the Spirit of God moved upon the waters: From <note>quoting Genesis 1:1–2</note>

In this third part of our sanctification, we experience the gifts of the Holy Spirit, through which we are able to become holy, righteous, and blessed. Because they are "Earths," and were made from the earth in the first beginning by **God** the **LORD**, just as with the other two lineages, the **Vegetables** <note>original: "Vegetabilia"</note> and the **Animals** <note>original: "Animalia"</note>; each is born from the earth, from its own seed. Furthermore, the earth must sustain and form them, which is then clearly revealed by the light of day. For the earth has the power of life within her, and whatever seed she catches, she breaks it down and unites herself with it, making the seed manifold—as a thousand grains come from a single little grain. Thus, the earth also bore a grain of that same kind, and those same little grains henceforth possess the power of the first grain.

# Thus, a detailed,

After the birth of Christ our **LORD** and Savior, in the year 1588, on the 14th day of August, this magnificent treatise was found in Danzig <note>Modern-day Gdańsk, Poland</note> in the Black Monks' Cloister of the Order of Preachers. <meta>This page continues the alchemical parable likely attributed to the philosopher Alphidius, following the description of the "old, single" truth or hero mentioned at the end of page 55. It provides the symbolic interpretation of the story's figures in relation to chemical processes.</meta>

...he gave the son a guide, and asked him to lead him well, and also to train him, so that no harm might come to him. Then the guide took the son and led him with him into the whole wide world onto the very highest mountain; there the guide showed the son all the treasures and riches of the world. Now when the son had seen everything, he began and spoke to the guide: "Come, and let us return, for I know that the father cannot live without us, and must die from great sorrow." When they returned, they found the father lying dead; then they immediately fell upon the father with weeping eyes and awakened him. Then he immediately became alive again, and with great joy he received them and kept them with him; thus they remained together and became one. 

This may now be compared and understood in a philosophical manner: it can be applied to God the Father in the Holy Trinity, or to a human being endowed with soul, spirit, flesh, and blood. Our **Matter** <note>The physical substance used at the start of the alchemical work.</note> is also interpreted in this way: for it has within itself <term>Gold ☉</term>, or Sulfur. In the **Putrefaction** <term>Putrefaction: The stage of "blackness" or decay where the matter is broken down.</term>, the **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note>—that is, the Father—is mortified <note>Killed or decomposed.</note> through the matter; then the hidden Son departs and travels out—that is, the Sulfur, the Soul, the Blood, acting as the Philosophical <term>Fire △</term>. The Guide is <term>Mercury ☿</term>, acting as the Spirit, the Breath, Smoke, and the <term>Water ▽</term>. 

The "World" is the glass or instrument; the "highest mountain" is the **Alembic** <term>Alembic: A capped vessel used in distillation to cool and condense vapors.</term>, into which all treasure and riches come. That which the son sees is the Father—as the matter, or the body, or the Salt and the dead earth—which remains lying at the bottom. The Guide, as Mercury, has the Son hidden within him—that is, the Sulfur and the **Soul** <note>original: *Animam*</note>. These two are cold and warm, moist and dry, <term>Water ▽</term> and <term>Fire △</term>, Soul and Spirit. As soon as they fall down upon the dead Father—which is the dry earth, the Body, the **Salt** <note>original: *Sal*</note>—with their rain or tears, the dead Father is refreshed and awakened again by his own Son and Guide; indeed, life is given to him, and with great joy he takes them back to himself and gladly keeps them with him. Also, these three remain together in one form and never allow themselves to be separated, etc.

### ARTEPHIUS ON THE SECRETS OF NATURE.

He taught that the Philosophers' Stone for making gold is such that it is neither combustible nor composed of combustible materials; its operation is easy, if you are able to ascend to the heights. For you shall take the *Green Lion* <term>Green Lion: A symbol for vitriol or a specific corrosive acid used to dissolve gold; it represents the raw, "hungry" state of the material.</term>, *white smoke*, and *stinking water*. Then dissolve it, make a lime <note>original: "calcem" — referring to calcination, the process of heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to powder.</note>, fix it, melt it, and sublime it, until the *red servant* is joined with the *white wife* <term>Red Servant and White Wife: Alchemical metaphors for the union of Sulfur (male/red) and Mercury (female/white) to produce the Stone.</term>. For when the lime that has been made turns white, and the sublimate <note>Sublimate: The solid deposit formed from a vapor during the process of sublimation.</note> flies away, the work is perfected.

In the name of God, understand / hear and pay attention / and take heed / you my most beloved friends / of the most supreme secret / which surpasses all the treasures of this entire world / and which God gives to His elect / and keeps hidden from the ignorant. Therefore, if you wish to attain this secret / which God the Father / and God the Son / and God the Holy Spirit has infused into you / then see to it / that you first seek the Kingdom of God and His righteousness / and then this gift shall be granted to you / and you will be filled with joy to see the wonderful power / which God has left in Nature through her works.

In all growing things / which are born in the earth / in the water / and above the earth / in the air and in the fire / there the first movement is **the Sun** <note>original: *SOL*. In alchemy, the Sun represents both the celestial body and the terrestrial metal, Gold.</note> / although nothing may be born / nor destroyed without the four elements / namely Heat and Cold / Dryness and Moisture / which Nature serves / and from her is thus born / and formed / many a wonderful shape according to the influence of the planets / whose images are imprinted upon them with a very different appearance: but rather in the quality of their **constitution** <term>complexion: a historical term referring to the specific balance of the four elements or humors in a body</term>. For we see / that in some things the four elements are in such balance / that none may have power over the others to rule in its constitution / as in pure **Gold** <note>original: *SOLE*</note> / and these we call healthy and perfect **bodies** <note>original: *CORPORA*</note>: But in others they are divided / and are consumed in the office of their dominance / but more so in Mars <note>iron</note> and Venus <note>copper</note> / and Jupiter <note>tin</note> and Saturn <note>lead</note> / and also otherwise in others. Thus are the stones / the **vitriols** <term>Atrament: a class of sulfate minerals, often used for making inks or in alchemical processes</term> / the **alums** <note>original: *Alumina*</note> and salt / and all **plants** <note>original: *Vegetabilia*</note> and **animals** <note>original: *Animalia*</note> / all of which are not found in the perfection of our meaning / upon which one cannot build: For they do not work in the pure essence / or the subtle nature / from which the body may become healthy. When these have lacked boiling for a long time, they become like the mother in their manner, but the weight of the father is retained. However, to unite them and to bring them into a **Solution**, that is difficult. For they are of a strong **Composition**, and each does not gladly depart from its own essence. For they could not be united by any reason: and were they not of one nature on account of their strong elements, they would be indestructible in themselves. But when they are mixed with one another, as will yet be revealed here, they no longer allow themselves to be separated, just as little as water is separated from water. For they either leave the fire entirely, or they remain entirely in the fire. For no element is divided from them, as was written before; and that is then the **Philosophers' Stone**, and the ***Two-fold Stone*** <note>original: *Lapis Rebis*. <margin>The middle soul between the Fixed and the Unfixed.</margin>
and our **Vinegar**, and **Magnesia**, and all the names of the **green trees**, and the middle between the **Fixed** and the **Unfixed**. But if one should say that the philosophers call it the "sharp water," that would be their vinegar, which makes the coarse small, the heavy light, the sharp mild, the hard soft, the sour sweet, the volatile constant; and when the elements are completely turned into one another, then one has the mastery entirely. This is thus to be understood: the sharp **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*.</note> that is sharp-cutting is made gentle through the **Solution**; thus it also becomes subtle and intangible, and is called **Volatile**, and afterwards becomes **Fixed**, as is written hereafter. And then the Master-builder shall consider that he must have a strong glass vessel. For all other vessels are not good, those made of earth or metals: and even if they were useful, they would still be of no use and unpleasant to the sight of the colors.

# XAMOLXIDES, &c.

When a highly understanding and wise **Philosopher** <note>original: *Philolophus*</note> wishes to begin the **Mysterial** work / he should honor the gods / and have daily **Conversation** <note>intercourse or communication</note> with spirits / and renounce this world / and live **contemplatively** / as I, Xamolxides, a lover of Jove <note>Jupiter</note>, do. ->Of the Carmelite Order, etc.<-

I am neither an evil nor a good angel, but rather I am one of the seven planetary spirits who rule over the Middle Nature <note>An esoteric concept referring to the intermediate realm between the divine/celestial and the physical/terrestrial</note>, who are commanded to govern the four distinct parts of the world, namely: the Firmamental, Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral parts. For the planets cannot come down in bodily form <note>original: *Corporalisch*</note>. **NB.** <note>Abbreviation for *Nota Bene*, meaning "Note Well"</note> This is the spirit who [governs] the internal birth-

I, BROTHER ALBERTUS Bayr, of the Carmelite Order <note>original: *Ordinis Carmelitani*</note>, do hereby affirm and testify before God and His angels and dear saints, that in the year 1568, on the 18th day of February—which was the feast of the glorious and highly blessed, ever-eternal Virgin Mary’s Candlemas <note>The feast of the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary, often associated in alchemy with the purification of matter.</note>—while I was in my cell in the monastery of Maria Magdalena of the New Star <note>original: *de Stella noua*</note>, such a vision appeared to me and held the aforementioned dialogue <note>original: *Colloquium*</note> with me. This occurred after I had risen and gone to bed day and night with philosophical books and thoughts, and prayed to God the Lord with fervent sighs day and night that He would graciously reveal to me the truth of this Art <note>Referring to the "Royal Art" of Alchemy.</note>. At that time, in my ignorance—may God forgive me—because I believed otherwise, after I had labored in vain with my Abbot for 23 years with great toil and diligently tended the fire day and night, [I believed] that one could learn the secret of these things from no human, but rather one must force it from the spirits—even though it is much more possible for humans than for spirits, as I, praise God, found in the end. 

Therefore, on the stated day, through customary ceremonies and proper conjurations <note>original: *Coniurationes*</note>—as is very common in monasteries in Italy and Spain—acting as a monastic exorcist <note>original: *Closter Exorcista*</note> (may God forgive me), I conjured the Spirit Qii <note>The name "Qii" is unusual; it may refer to a specific spirit of Mercury or a coded name used in this particular manuscript tradition.</note> and demanded a conversation: who appeared to me in the form of a black, elongated, frightening glow or shadow, without any form or shape of a human or animal, and gave me question and answer with a resounding, echoing voice, as reported before.

And when, at his command, I seated myself at the table, having prepared myself with pen and ink, that same shadow or black glow stepped into the center of the circle, regardless of the consecrated sword, censed candles, and other hocus-pocus <note>original: *Gauckelwerck*; referring to the ritual tools of ceremonial magic, which the spirit notably ignores.</note>. Afterward, it transformed from the black color through an ash-colored gray cloud into an entirely bright white glow, and finally changed from the white through a light yellow color into the highest redness <note>These colors—black, white, yellow, and red—represent the four major stages of the alchemical process: *Nigredo* (blackening), *Albedo* (whitening), *Citrinitas* (yellowing), and *Rubedo* (reddening).</note>. But the form and size did not reverse or change, but remained standing quite unmoved in the circle until the end of the conversation; however, in the center of the glow, the sign ☿ <note>The symbol for Mercury.</note> stood in three distinct colors. Finally, when he disappeared as described, my cell appeared and became blood-red inside and out, just as the sun is wont to shine blood-red into a room.

After this revelation, I arranged everything with my Abbot. Within two years, we produced eleven pounds and seven lots <note>A 'lot' (German: *Lot*) was a unit of weight, roughly equivalent to 1/32 of a pound or about 15-16 grams.</note> of the true matter <note>original: *Matery*</note> with great toil and diligence. My Abbot, however, did not live to see it; for on the 2nd of June prior, he was found dead in bed alongside his concubine <note>original: *Concubina*</note>. From beginning to end, I saw all the colors, and just as the spirit <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> appeared in the circle, so too I found the three primary colors <note>original: *Hauptfarben*</note>—namely black, white, and red—distinctly within the Work. Whenever a single error occurred, I always received good counsel and instruction from the aforementioned spirit. In particular, he explained the parable of the fountain <note>original: *Fontina*</note> of Bernard <note>Refers to Bernard of Trevisan, a 15th-century alchemist famous for his allegorical "Parable of the Fountain" describing the stages of the alchemical process.</note> to me in such a way that afterwards all the hidden writings and figures of the Chaldeans, Egyptians, and other philosophers became clear to me, as I have recorded—mostly in my own blood—in the fourth part of my little book which I wrote about the Book of Bernard.

But after the completion of the Work, I was unable to call the spirit back to me for several years. Therefore, the augmentation <note>original: *Augmentatio*; the process of increasing the quantity or potency of the alchemical medicine.</note> in power and quantity <note>original: *in Virtute & Quantitate*</note> proved very difficult for me. Because I received no further instruction or report from the spirit, and the other brothers—especially the new Abbot—were very hostile and opposed to me because they could learn nothing from me regarding these matters, I secretly slipped away a few years later with my tincture <note>original: *Tinctur*; the transformative alchemical substance, often called the Philosopher's Stone.</note> and several good old Egyptian books. I arrived safely in Augsburg and afterward traveled to Nuremberg, being glad to finally reach German soil, held by the comforting hope that I might eventually find someone who would show me the process of augmentation. May God Almighty further help everyone with His grace; highly praised and lauded into all eternity, Amen, Amen.

# COLLOQUY
## or Dialogue between Nature, MERCURY, and an Alchemist.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'E' featuring scrolling vine and floral motifs.</image-desc>

Once upon a time, chemists <note>original: *Chymisten*; in this period, the terms "chemist" and "alchemist" were often used interchangeably for those studying the transformation of matter.</note> gathered and held counsel on how the PHILOSOPHERS' STONE <note>original: *LAPIDEM PHILOSOPHORVM*; the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and providing an elixir of life.</note> might be prepared. They decided among themselves that each should offer his own opinion on the matter. This assembly took place under the open sky, upon a heath, and on a very clear day. There, many agreed unanimously that quicksilver or Mercury <note>original: *Mercurius*; in alchemy, Mercury is one of the three primary principles (Tria Prima) along with Sulphur and Salt.</note> was the First Matter; others, however, believed it to be Sulphur, while others proposed something else entirely. Nevertheless, Mercury or quicksilver was primarily discussed, especially from the writings of the Philosophers <note>Referring to the ancient and medieval authorities on alchemy, such as Hermes Trismegistus or Geber.</note>, since they present it as the true Matter, as well as the First Matter of metals. For the Philosophers cry out and shout: "Our Mercury! Our Quicksilver!" etc. While they were thus contending and struggling with great effort (for each was eager for the final resolution of this question), a severe storm suddenly arose with thunder, lightning, and hail, along with unprecedented winds and downpours. This violence scattered the assembly, casting each one into different foreign lands and provinces, dividing and completely separating them, so that the final conclusion and closing statement was prevented and remained unfinished at that time.

Nevertheless, in the time that followed, each man imagined for himself what the final outcome of this dispute and debate might be. Therefore, each one set to work and began to seek the Philosophers' Stone—one in this matter, another in that—which continues to happen incessantly even to this day. But one among them in particular, still mindful of the conversation they had held—namely, that the Stone of the Wise <note>original: *Stein der Weisen*; another name for the Philosophers' Stone.</note> was to be prepared from Mercury or quicksilver—spoke these words to himself: "Although no final conclusion...

# AUGUSTINE TO THE SWEET-SPEAKER.
<note>original: "AVGVSTINVS DVLCILOQVIO." This likely refers to a collection of "sweet sayings" or a specific addressed discourse attributed to St. Augustine, frequently cited in alchemical texts to provide a moral and theological foundation for the work.</note>
## Book 3.

Seek the Lord, and your soul shall live. Let the earth bring forth a living soul. Do not be conformed to this world: restrain yourselves from it. By avoiding the world, the Soul lives, which by desiring it dies. Restrain yourselves from the monstrous ferocity of pride: from the sluggish pleasure of luxury: and from the deceptive name of knowledge. For the haughtiness of elation, the delight of lust, and the poison of curiosity are the movements of a dying soul—which does not die in such a way as to lack all life, but because by departing from the fountain of life it dies, and is taken up by the passing world and conformed to it. But your Word is the Fountain of eternal life, and it does not pass away. But be transformed in the novelty of your mind to prove what is the will of God: that which is good, well-pleasing, and perfect, etc.

## DEDICATORY ELEGY TO THE MOST NOBLE, MOST GRAVE, MOST LEARNED, AND MOST EXPERIENCED IN THE <term>SPAGYRIC ART</term>, LORD JOHANN BAPTIST VON SEEBACH, ETC. GENTLEMAN-AT-TABLE TO THE HOLY ROMAN IMPERIAL MAJESTY OF RUDOLPH II, EMPEROR, ETC. HIS MOST WORSHIPFUL PATRON AND MAECENAS.

Thrice-noble Star of the Seebach lineage, JOHANN

When we look back upon the sages of former times, the minds of them all were directed toward recognizing the hidden things of nature, bringing them to light, and enlightening the darkened human understanding through wisdom; since man surpasses other animals in no other way than when he, in his enlightened understanding, contemplates nature as it is enclosed within the circles of the heavens, and brings forth natural works in accordance with such wise contemplation. Therefore, all philosophers and sages have endeavored to ensure that their successors would be nourished with the wisdom and understanding of nature, and not remain stuck in ignorance and darkness of the mind, through which they step away from human perfection toward the strange, wild nature of irrational animals. For this reason, there are many kinds of books by many learned and wise people available, in which each has explained and revealed his conceived or otherwise learned wisdom according to his ability and pleasure, and shown us by what means, manner, and way we also could attain such intended wisdom: so that we might not perhaps miss the right goal of wisdom and be led into various detours.

And although the philosophers have used various ways of speaking about a single thing, so that one might think there is no *consensus* <note>original: "Consensum" — agreement or harmony.</note> in their writings, and therefore nothing thorough to be found: yet one must take good heed and know that only one <term>Naturist</term> <note>In this context, a "Naturist" refers to a singular, vital power or "universal spirit" that governs all natural processes.</note> is spread throughout all creatures of the world, which maintains each species in its own place and its own kind, and lets nothing happen by chance, but rather everything stands and exists in *Number, Weight, and Measure* <note>original: "Numero, Pondere & Mensura." A common alchemical and theological reference to the Wisdom of Solomon 11:20: "Thou hast ordered all things in measure and number and weight."</note>. Since this is so, as Holy Scripture along with experience testifies, even though the philosophers have not spoken uniformly, it will therefore

...nothing is taken from unique Nature itself, which is not bound to this or that writing, but exists for itself without writing. This is sufficiently obvious to those who strive to explore it not only with skillful, lofty thoughts but also with practical, diligent, and clever works. Therefore, every person must take great care that they do not perhaps let Nature slip away and devote themselves solely to the books of the philosophers, from which they will draw all sorts of opinions; it would then be difficult for them to distinguish these from one another and to pick out the right and true ones from the bad and incorrect ones. Thus, Nature must be taken in hand along with and alongside reading, and reading along with and alongside Nature; reading must be judged from Nature, and not Nature from reading. Even though the difficult writings of highly learned philosophers lead one a good way toward the knowledge of Nature and are, so to speak, a *guiding hand* <note>original: "Manuductio"; a Latin term for an introduction or a "leading by the hand."</note>. 

For in the contemplation of Nature—after the philosophers first viewed the heavens and their constellations, along with their constant motion, and then the four *elements* <note>original: "Elementa"</note> and what is within them—they found that the heavens have an effect on the elements, and one element on another. It is as if the heavens command and rule the elements, just as a father does his son; hence, they considered and wrote that the heavens are necessary *for generation* <note>original: "ad Generationem"; referring to the creation or reproduction of life and matter</note>. From this also comes the common philosophical proverb: *The Sun and man beget man* <note>original: "Sol & Homo generant Hominem"; a traditional Aristotelian concept suggesting that human life requires both biological parents and the life-giving energy of the sun.</note>. Indeed, they have also finely divided their writings, based on the workings of Nature, into *celestial things, animals, vegetables, and minerals* <note>original: "Cœlestia, Animalia, Vegetabilia & Mineralia"</note>, because they believed that under these four parts almost all things subject to Nature were comprised. 

They have also assigned to each thing its property and effect according to its kind, and held each in the high status in which it was placed by God. For in the heavens, they paid particular attention to the great light which was placed over the day by God Himself at the creation of the world—namely, the sun. Not that other celestial glowing bodies are not also stars or do not have their own particular effects, but that the sun far surpasses them all in clarity, perfection of its shine, motion, and effect in Nature, as it receives its light from no other star, but all others are illuminated by the sun; without this illumination, they are dark and dull bodies. Likewise, the air is purified by the *solar rays* <note>original: "Radios Solares"</note>, the plants of the earth are lured forth and refreshed, and each is brought to its perfection; similarly, all animals rejoice in the sun,

However, since it is also obvious that the Sun cannot illuminate or refresh any creature that withdraws from its brilliance and power; and wine cannot gladden the heart of one who does not use it; and Mummy cannot keep anyone alive from whose body it is separated: so it is also impossible for gold to give strength to the heart (in which lies the foundation of human life) unless these two—namely, gold and the heart—are united in such a way that one can work upon the other. Therefore, they sought a certain way by which the essential power could be extracted from the <term>solar body</term> <note>original: "$\odot$ischen Leichnam"; the physical, "dead" husk of the metal</note> and separated from it. This happens for no other reason than **because the species of things are distinct by specific differences, and are preserved in their Being through the succession of subsequent individuals** <note>original: "quia Species Rerum per differentias specificas sunt distinctæ, ac per successionem subeuntium individuorum in suo ESSE conseruantur"</note>. 

Since this is so, no **Vegetable** <note>original: "Vegetabile," referring to the plant kingdom</note> will give birth to an **Animal** <note>original: "Animale"</note>, nor any Animal to a **Mineral** <note>original: "Minerale"</note>; rather, each will bring forth within its own kind <note>original: "in suo genere"</note> what is implanted in its seed to bring forth: the Vegetable brings forth something vegetable, the Animal something animal, the Mineral something mineral. As an example: no human will give birth to a herb, or a tree, or a metal. Likewise, no tree or herb will give birth to a human or a metal. Thus, also, no metal will give birth to a human or a tree, but each will be preserved in its own race and therein bring forth fruit: metal begets metal, humans beget humans, herbs beget herbs, and so on. **For species differing in genus can never be confused or mixed, but differ from one another more by a generic difference than species of the same genus differ from each other by their own constitutive difference.** <note>original: "Nam genere differentes Species nunquam confundi possunt aut queunt, sed sub suo genere à se mutuo differunt magis differentia Generica, qua ejusdem generis Species inter se differunt sua differentia seipsam constitutiua." This Scholastic argument emphasizes that the fundamental categories of life and matter do not mix.</note>

Similarly, there is a greater difference between metals and animals than there is between a human and an ape. There is also a small question here among those who are not thoroughly experienced in Nature: what kind of fire <note>original symbol: △</note> must this be, in which this third sublimation <note>original: ~tion</note> or putrefaction <term>putrefactio; the state of alchemical decay</term>, or the resolution of Mercury into Water (which are all one thing), must be accomplished? For this reason, it will be necessary to ask the Philosophers and those experienced in the Art, who unanimously show us that it is a *vaporous fire of the horse's belly* <note>original: vaporosus ignis ventris Equini; referring to the gentle, steady heat produced by fermenting horse manure</note>. Therefore, Arnoldus speaks in the *Rosary*:

> The fire of dung is the active cause in the work of digesting our Stone, nor is the fire of the Bath of Mary <note>original: Balnei Marię; a water bath or bain-marie</note> of any use, even if it is very well-tempered.

Therefore Alphidius also speaks:

> To cook with fire, which I shall show you, is namely to hide [the vessel] in moist horse dung, which is the moist and dark fire of the Sages; it is hot in the second degree and moist in the first degree. The property of this fire is not to destroy the Oil—that is, the matter—but it increases it because of its tempered moisture. For that heat alone is equal and temperate, and such is highly necessary in the generation of this thing.

From these words, it is understood not only what kind of fire <note>original symbol: △</note> must be used for this work, but also what kind of furnace, and what degree of fire—namely, an equal, tempered degree, through which nothing is destroyed, but the entire Mercury is transformed into a Water <note>original symbol: ▽</note> through the action of the vaporous Air. Therefore, all other fires besides this one are useless and an automated hindrance to the completion of the Tincture; this is especially to be noted, so that no obstacle falls in the way and one does not fail to reach the desired end. For the *Assembly of Philosophers* <note>original: Turba; referring to the *Turba Philosophorum*, one of the oldest Latin alchemical texts</note> does not speak in vain:

> In all things it is a marvel that by one fire, and one vessel, there occurs distillation, sublimation <note>original: ~tion</note>, mortification, calcination, whitening, reddening, and fusion, with all solutions and coagulations.

It is also necessary that the instrument in which the glass is to stand be prepared with diligence, so that the glass in which the Mercury is sealed can be conveniently placed upon a tripod with cotton...

Gold appears entirely as Gold; all its parts are red. Nevertheless, it is transformed into the **whitish eagle** <note>original: "weißlechten Adler"; a symbolic name for the white, volatile stage of the substance</note>, so that it loses its redness. So too the whitish eagle, or the **Mercury of the Sun**, appears entirely white; yet beneath it, the highest redness of Gold remains hidden, as the work itself finally clearly demonstrates and brings forth. Therefore, the Philosophers rightly said: the outermost part of Gold is the innermost part of Mercury—since the outermost of Gold is red, and the innermost hidden part of Mercury is also red. Conversely, the outermost part of Mercury is the innermost part of Gold—since the outermost of Mercury is white, and the innermost part of Gold is also white. It is indeed transformed into the whitish eagle and Mercury, which could not happen if its nature were not directed toward that end.

In the same way, this Mercury is resolved into a water, and afterwards this water—as mentioned—becomes a citrine-colored oil, identical in color to the **peels of pomegranates**. This is the true **Fixed Sulfur of the Sun**. If one wished to use this as a medicine, it is unspeakable what it can achieve; a single drop of this colors an entire measure of wine and even more, which is then the best **Potable Gold** <term>Aurum Potabile; a legendary liquid medicine believed to grant longevity</term>, beyond which none better can be found.

...to proceed with both **putrefactions**, then this **citrine-brown oil** begins to change into another kind, and a small skin forms on top, which then falls to the bottom, and soon another comes again, and falls to the bottom once more, like a yellowish, subtle sand; and this happens for as long as it takes for all the oil to become a powder and turn into a yellowish sand. When all this has shown itself in this way, the heat of the fire should not be decreased, but continued; then the yellow powder begins to become grayish, and the longer it goes, the more it leans toward blackness, until finally it becomes completely black, and shows itself as the **Raven's Head** <term>Raven’s Head; the alchemical stage of "nigredo" or blackening, symbolizing the death and purification of the matter</term>, which then is a good sign, and an end of the true destruction, and a beginning of the right **tincture** <term>tincture; the transformative essence capable of changing metals</term>.

Therefore the **Assembly of Philosophers** <note>original: Turba Philosophorum; one of the oldest and most influential Latin alchemical texts</note> says: *“Here the bodies are dissolved through putrefaction, and are made into a black earth: and when you see the matter blackened, rejoice, for it is the beginning of the work, and it is the black of the white, and the head of the raven, which flies without wings in the clarity of night and day.”* <note>original Latin: "Hic soluta sunt corpora per putrefactionem, & efficiuntur terra nigra..."</note> And further: *“This is the black and dark Earth of which the Philosophers speak, saying: Be therefore diligent in the operation in all its states, patiently continuing the boiling until the Tincture comes out upon the water in a black color, and when you see the blackness looming over that water, know that the whole body is liquefied, and then it is necessary to continue a gentle fire until it conceives the cloud which it bears in darkness.”* <note>original Latin: "Ista est Terra nigra & tenebrosa..."</note>

From these words it clearly follows that the blackness in this work must initially appear after the **calcination** <term>calcination; heating a substance until it is reduced to a dry powder</term>, which then afterwards is also not permanent, but changes into another kind. Therefore the Philosophers have invented the idea that this blackness is a **Raven**, which flies without wings as well in the brightness of the night as in the clarity of the day; by the night and the day they give us to understand the change that occurs within the blackness. 

So since the blackness is also to be transformed into something else, one must investigate here with no small diligence into what this change must occur. Therefore, the Philosophical saying should be considered here, in which it is said: *“That heat acting on the moist generates blackness, and acting on the dry generates whiteness.”* <note>original: "Quod calor agens in humidum generat nigredinem, & agens in siccum generat albedinem."</note> Since this black matter or **Raven's Head**, or **Blacker than Black** <note>original: Nigrum nigrius nigro</note>, or whatever one wishes to call it, was previously an ash-colored earth, and this a yellowish powder, this powder a citrine-brown oil, the oil a water—which water then first appeared in the resolution of the **Mercury of the Sun** <term>Mercury of the Sun; the spiritual or metallic essence of gold</term>, and was first transformed into the citrine-brown oil, the citrine-brown oil then into a yellowish powder, the yellowish powder into an ash-colored earth, then into a black earth—it follows that this black earth also

...on white / the red on red. Of the white **Tincture** <term>Tincture; in alchemy, a substance capable of transmuting or "dyeing" base metals into noble ones</term> the Philosophers write: that it transforms all imperfect bodies into the purest **Silver**, better than that from the mine. <note>original Latin: "quod transformet omnia corpora imperfecta in purissimum Argentum, melius quàm à minera"</note> Therefore truly a great secret is indicated here, which is not to be revealed to any wicked person, but is to be kept in secrecy among the Philosophers alone; for this Art of bringing the lesser metals into higher ones—the imperfect into perfect—is nothing else, if it comes to an evil person, than a sword in a madman's hand, who carelessly causes harm to everyone.

For this reason, one must deal with it quietly and discreetly, and pray to God for grace, that He may grant success to it: For this is indeed a great thing, that Art here far surpasses Nature, in that the silver prepared through Art is more perfect than that which is taken out of the Earth—as understood in the Philosophical saying—and yet such a thing can be accomplished through an easy Art; therefore the Philosophers write further: **Whiten therefore the Laton <term>Laton; an alchemical term for the "base" or impure matter (often associated with copper or brass) that must be purified</term>, and tear up the books, lest your hearts be torn, because our art is light, and requires light assistance.** <note>original Latin: "Dealbate ergò Latonem, & libros rumpite, ne rumpantur corda vestra, quia ars nostra leuis est, & leui indiget subsidio"</note> 

But although the Art is easy and requires a light assistance, it should be diligently noted here that this light assistance and light Art are not easily obtained: For even though the white Tincture or **Medicine** <term>Medicine; another name for the Elixir or Philosopher's Stone, which "heals" the "sickness" of base metals</term> is ready, it cannot yet be used unless it is first brought to enter the **Bodies** <term>Bodies; the base metals to be transformed</term> through more convenient ways and means; because it has been cleansed and clarified of all superfluities and impurities, it is of a much higher nature than other metals, which is the reason why it does not enter or unite with the metals at all without the preparation of the **Arcanum** <term>Arcanum; a deep secret or a powerful transformative substance</term>, as you will then be taught in the red Medicine. 

If, however, no color appears after the white (as mentioned) except for the Redness, it would be ill-advised to use the white Tincture since the Redness follows easily: It is also not necessary to take a special path here, **Because the White and the Red proceed from one root**, as Arnold <note>likely referring to Arnaldus de Villa Nova, a 13th-century physician and alchemist</note> testifies: but it requires only a longer time and constant cooking. 

One cannot err with the fire **after the whiteness, because in this whiteness the REDNESS is hidden**, <note>original Latin: "Post albedinem, quia in hac albedine RUBOR est occultus"</note> which Redness must then be brought forth solely through longer cooking. **Therefore, let it be cooked with dry fire** (as the *Assembly of the Philosophers* <term>Turba Philosophorum; one of the oldest and most famous alchemical texts in Latin, presented as a debate among sages</term> says) **and dry calcination, until it becomes red like Cinnabar <term>Cinnabar; mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral</term>; to which cooking you should by no means add water, nor any other thing, until the Red is cooked to completion; it will give the eternal color of Gold.** <note>original Latin: "Igne igitur sicco (ut ait Turba Philosophor.) & calcinatione sicca decoquatur, donec rubeat ut Cinabrium, cui decoctioni nequaquam imponas aquam, neq; aliam rem, quousq; ad complementum coquatur Rubeum, dabit Colorem Auri perpetuum."</note> 

Hence are these certain old Rhymes:

> So that the **ROSE** does not just glow white, but shines with light,
> Let it only boil constantly, and rest in the heat.

And such Multiplying can happen for a third time because of the unspeakable expansion of the weight found in the calculation. Therefore, one cannot marvel enough at such **Great Wonders of God** <note>original: "Magnalibus Dei"</note>; and it is also certainly true that there have been many among the Philosophers who possessed the **Blessed Stone** <note>original: "Lapidem Benedictum"</note> and brought it to a happy end, but among them few who knew the Ingress. Indeed, there were also many of them who, although they knew the Ingress, did not discover the Multiplication.

Therefore, every Philosopher to whom such a high and magnificent **Gift of God** <note>original: "Donum Dei"</note>—which exists in Nature—is granted by God, should handle it with secrecy. For Solomon the Wise himself says: **"The wise hide knowledge, but the mouth of the fool is near to confusion."** <note>original Latin: "Sapientes abscondit scientian, os autem Stulti confusioni est proximum." A reference to Proverbs 10:14</note> Therefore, one cannot wonder enough, nor is it unjust, why such great secrets in Nature have always remained so hidden by the Philosophers; for they by no means wanted them to fall into the hands of the ignorant.

# The Little Book of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), a famous Swiss physician and alchemist.</note> with the Heavenly Bagpipes, Dedicated to a Princely Person.

In God’s name, I wish to tell Your Princely Grace <note>original: "E. F. Gn." (Euer Fürstlichen Gnaden); a standard formal address for royalty or high nobility.</note> the true secret of the philosophers, which the wise have kept hidden for a long time, and have told only through parables, as the philosopher Geber <note>Geber is the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a legendary 8th-century Islamic alchemist whose writings were foundational to European alchemy.</note> speaks of.

A fellow went along, like one who seeks something, or has lost his way; he traveled so far that it was perilous to turn back, and he pressed on so far until he came into a lovely pleasure garden, in which trees stood with many branches, adorned with many kinds of fruit. These fruits refreshed the fellow so that he partially forgot his sorrowful mind and pressed on even further. Then he came to a beautiful castle that belonged to a King who had six daughters, who were meant to wait upon and guard the house and the garden. And as he came to the first gate, he was met by a red man, very ugly and misshapen, who nonetheless spoke to him with mild words, asking what he sought there, for he had never found anyone so close to the house. He gave him the answer and said: he sought the Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: "Lapidem Philosophorum"; the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>. The red man said to him: "Because you have come so far, I will guide you further; you shall go until you come to a yellow man. He will be mild with you in all his dealings; though he looks ugly, his words are friendly. He will also ask you questions; tell him I have directed you to him, and he will guide you further." And when he came to the yellow man, the same asked him where he came from, for he had never seen any man so close there. Then the seeker spoke: He sought the Philosopher’s Stone, and a red man had directed him there. Then the yellow man said: "Since you have come so far, I will guide you further," and said: "As you come further inside, you will come to a springing fountain; from it, you shall receive a glass full, which is called Virgin's Milk <note>original: "Lac Virginis"; a symbolic alchemical term usually referring to a mercurial solvent or a specific stage in the purification of matter.</note>, and you shall take that with you. And you shall go further, and you will come to a black raven, in which a white dove is hidden. The raven is quite untamed; he bites and scratches gladly, and has a stinking breath. Now, my dearest friend," spoke the yellow man, "how will you bring the white dove out of the black raven—

### The Second Practice

Furthermore, let Your Princely Grace take, in the name of the Lord, the purified high vinegar as described above in a strong glass, and set it in ashes <note>An ash-bath or *balneum cineris*, used to provide gentle, even heat.</note>, well-stopped and sealed all around so that it stands immovable and is not disturbed until the end of the work; and pay special attention to the weight. 

To this, take of the strong vinegar and add an equal weight of the sweet water that has been purified as stated above. Fix a helm upon it and withdraw <note>original: *detrahirt*; to draw off or distill away.</note> the sweet ▽ <note>water</note> from it. The vinegar will remain at the bottom, for it is heavy and does not easily rise. When the glass has cooled, give the drawn-off ▽ <note>water</note> back to it, and draw it off again. Repeat this pouring-on and drawing-off <note>This process of repeated distillation is known as "reiteration" or "cohabitation."</note> so often until the vinegar becomes a crystal in the color of a beautiful ruby; this Your Princely Grace shall see when the glass becomes cold. 

Now Your Princely Grace has a human and metallic medicine which, after its justification and preparation, converts all metals into gold, as you know; this is certain. But if you should run short of the sweet water—which is not likely—then prepare more as you did at the beginning and give it to the stone, which is called the "growing stone." It is without end, and you require no ferment <note>A substance added to a mixture to complete a transformation; here, the "stone" is self-sufficient.</note> in its composition and birth.

### Here the black raven now releases the white dove from itself.

Now let Your Princely Grace <note>addressed to Joachim Ernst, Margrave of Brandenburg-Ansbach.</note> take the reserved black earth and calcine <note>To heat a substance to high temperatures in a furnace until it is reduced to a dry powder or ash.</note> it in a wind furnace <note>A furnace designed to create a natural draft to reach high temperatures.</note> for about 4 hours, until it becomes entirely black. This pouring on and drawing off shall be done 7 times. After that, calcine the earth for 2 or 3 hours, then grind it small and very fine. Pour the sweet water over it again, seal the top of the vessel well, and place it in a gentle heat for about 5 or 6 hours. After that, filter it as finely as possible. Keep what has been filtered; and whatever has not yet dissolved, pour more sweet water over it. Continue this until the Salt is entirely pure and filtered. You must do this until the Salt has completely dissolved; otherwise, it would not be good or prepared for your Work. Then your purified earth is well-prepared and processed.

When that is done, give it the sweet water again and dissolve it completely as before. Once it is dissolved, distill it again over the helm until it becomes dry. ## USE OF THE OIL.

The Oil <note>original: "Oleum"</note>, taken with good Malmsey wine <note>A sweet, potent wine from Greece or the Canary Islands, often used as a vehicle for medicines.</note> or in Pimpernel water in the morning on an empty stomach, creates a joyful heart and purifies the blood and leprosy <note>original: "Aussatz," which historically referred to many chronic skin conditions.</note>.

Also: It preserves the natural heat and increases it. Also, used with Fumitory water <note>original: "Erdrauchwasser," a plant historically used for skin ailments and liver health.</note>, it cleanses leprosy. Also, taken with Betony water, it takes away gray hair and brings back beautiful hair. Also, used with Marjoram water <note>original: "Maioran ▽." The triangle symbol represents Water.</note>, it takes away pains of the head and kills the gray hairs in the head, etc.

## ->A NOTE on the Philosopher’s Stone.<-

The **Philosopher's Stone** <note>original: Lapis Philosophorum</note> is thus recognized and revealed through the high understanding of the Sages, left here for us. Note this: once you have brought this stone to its highest perfection, you must protect the treasure from the air and feed it with **Gold** <note>Symbol: ☉; the text uses the Latin *Solem*, literally "the Sun."</note> as soon as the clarity of this perfect end has been seen. Otherwise, if it were to remain **on its own** <note>original: per se</note> for too long, it would eat and attack itself—yes, consume itself entirely—and through that, what was gained would be lost.

For as soon as this stone is born and has become manifest, it is entirely heavenly and also spiritual; therefore, give it food and **Ferment** quickly, using the **Sun** as a meal. TREATISE III. ON THE P. S. <note>original: L. P., abbreviation for *Lapis Philosophorum* or Philosophers' Stone</note>

<image-desc>An ornamental headpiece with symmetrical, scrolling acanthus-style foliate designs.</image-desc>

# Here follows a proper, thorough, and true description by Caspar Hartung of the Court in Vogtland, etc., Theologian and Philosopher, etc., concerning the preparation of the blessed Stone, together with its Subject; its nature and essence, proven with beautiful figures and Holy Scripture, etc.

## Preface.

<image-desc>An ornamental woodcut initial letter 'E' decorated with scrolling foliage.</image-desc>
It is to be known that all things come from God, and without Him nothing can be made, as you find in Genesis 1 and in the Gospel of John 1. Therefore, in all our actions, we should call upon God and ask Him for reason and understanding for this holy work, as all the Philosophers say—such as Hermes, Arnoldus de Villa Nova, and [Basil] Valentine—and John at the end [of his Gospel], stating that such things must be learned from God. We should not proceed with our own stubborn minds, thinking we can force our way through, regardless of whether God allows nature to endure it or not; they <note>referring to "false" alchemists or "souphuffers"</note> do not take that into account, but simply push forward. One says it is hidden in wine; another, in imperfect bodies <note>meaning base metals like lead or tin</note>; in blood; in marcasites <term>marcasite: a term then used for various metallic ores, often iron pyrite</term>; in Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note>; in sulfur; in salt <note>original symbol: □; likely referring to common salt or saltpeter</note>; in urine; in Antimony <note>original symbol: ♁</note>; in Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note>; in orpiment <term>orpiment: a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</term>; and in herbs, such as Celandine, Caper Spurge, Ivy, etc. It is all together roguery and thievery, with which they lead people astray and rob them of their money; they consume and lose things in vain and uselessly, following only their own foolish heads, which cannot even calculate beforehand what the need requires. Dear friend, tell me one thing: who must [be] in the minerals of the ear...

...burn the Strong Water <note>original: AqF., likely *Aqua Fortis*, often used by alchemists to refer to nitric acid or distilled spirits</note>, or are there people within who distill wine, or use child’s urine to produce metals? Or do you think there are apothecaries within who have all things for sale, so that you can make **lead, tin, silver, gold, copper, iron?** You fool! Can you not understand that you are mistaken? None of these things belong to the ways of Nature. Or do you wish to be above God? 

If you want to make metal out of blood, then you might as well make a man out of a horse, or a cow out of a mouse—one that might even give you good milk! That would indeed be a **multiplication** <term>multiplication: in alchemy, the process of increasing the power, weight, or quantity of the Philosophers' Stone</term>. But it does not happen; and just as little as those things can occur, just as little can you make metal for me out of the things mentioned above. 

If you wish to make metals, however, then pay closer attention to the **Philosophers**, and how they teach you to understand **Nature**; for the **Art** <note>meaning the "Alchemical Art"</note> is nothing more than Nature itself. What Nature has not created, Art can have no effect upon. For when a woman gives birth to a little boy, you will not be able to make a little girl out of him with your Art; whatever you may add to the matter will not help you. Likewise, no **laxative** can purge a dead person; but as long as there is still a nature within a person, then the Art can assist Nature—such as by keeping warm, eating good things, etc. 

Therefore, I ask you, if you wish to be a **Philosopher**, prepare yourself for it and follow my well-intentioned teaching, which I offer you in all faithfulness. You shall hear more of this hereafter in my book, following the consensus of all the Philosophers who truly possessed the Art, and as I myself have seen and performed it. Open your understanding, study, and read over this often; for truly, the Art cannot be learned or understood except through **God**, or a learned Master and Philosopher. The entirety of **Holy Scripture** touches upon this, as you will see through both writings and figures <note>referring to alchemical illustrations</note>. I shall prove it to you with honest, recognizable reasons drawn from the Scripture and from my Masters, the **Philosophers**. I do this so that you may not say hereafter that they did not write it for you correctly; the fault lies in whether you understand it rightly, for they warn you sufficiently—such as **Hermes**, a father [of the Art], and the...

The authority of the philosophers, and first: **Eſſret** <note>This likely refers to an Arabic alchemical authority, possibly a corrupted spelling of Rhazes (Al-Razi) or a specific commentator on Geber.</note> says clearly: The coagulable quicksilver and the living, sulfurous quicksilver are the first materials of metal. For all other moistures perish and vanish easily through the fire, and one element separates from the other, just as water is affected by fire: one part dissolves into the air as steam, and the other remains as earth at the bottom of the vessel. And thus the elements of all things separate, for they are not well-united in a stable essence; and no matter how small a fire you make, or what substance you add to it, it consumes itself and separates from its natural composition. 

But concerning the **viscous moisture**—the "flow"—it is never consumed, nor does it separate from its earth, nor from its other elements; for either the whole of it remains, or the whole of it flies away. And he says that this is the thing that unites with the metal at its very root, breaks its imperfect form, and leads it into another form according to its color.

...a great multitude of those in error, who desire to confirm their delusion and to testify that the four elements are the first Matter of metal. 

Furthermore: One might also argue against me, or oppose me and turn all my answers against me, saying: if we reduce the four elements back [to their essence], and thereafter according to our Art <note>In this context, "Art" refers to the skilled practice of alchemy or chemistry.</note> turn them into <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: *Mercurium*</note> and <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original: *Sulphur*</note>, then these are the first Matter of the metals. I will prove that this is erroneous and false through many necessary reasons, so that I may stop their mouths once and for all and put an end to their wicked designs; and also so that it is not said that I correct others according to my own whim, but rather with sound reasoning. 

Therefore I tell you: if this were true, it would not be necessary for any Nature to exist. The reason being that Art would then make the Seed of all things—and of humans—from the elements alone, without Nature; and without any [natural] change, Art would make the beginning of the composition. This is against all understanding, for Nature brings forth, and has brought forth, and only thereafter has Art helped her. 

It would also follow that a Physician <note>original: *Medicus*</note> through his art of herbs would awaken a dead man, or that he should make a dying human healthy, which is against the words of <term>Avicenna</term> <note>A Persian polymath (c. 980–1037) regarded as one of the most significant physicians and thinkers of the Islamic Golden Age.</note> and <term>Rhazes</term> <note>Abu Bakr al-Razi (865–925), a Persian physician and chemist who pioneered clinical medicine.</note>, where they say: <term>Medicine</term> is only a helper to Nature; for where Nature is not present, Medicine can have no effect. Just as a laxative in a dead body does not purge, because it is not directed according to Nature. For thus says <term>Hippocrates</term> <note>The ancient Greek "Father of Medicine."</note> in his <term>Aphorisms</term> <note>original: *Aphorimis*</note>: Art only prepares a thing already created by Nature and provides it with help; and Art helps this Matter, and Nature helps Art.

# The IV. Chapter.

## The first strong water **OF THE PHILOSOPHERS** <note>original: "PHILOSOPHORVM"</note>.

**Take Roman Vitriol** <term>Roman Vitriol: Usually copper sulfate or iron sulfate, used as a primary ingredient in creating mineral acids.</term> half a pound, 2 and a half [units] of beautifully purified **Saltpeter** <term>🜔: The alchemical symbol for Saltpeter (Nitre), a key oxidizing agent.</term> and 1 pound of burnt **Gold** <term>☉: The symbol for the Sun or Gold. And that is the first water / of which you must have 3 or 4 pounds for our work. The signs of this water are / that it dissolves **Silver** <term>☾: The symbol for the Moon or Silver.</term>, it separates **Gold** <term>☉</term> and **Silver** <term>☾</term>, it turns Mercury into a **Crocus** <term>Crocus: A term for a fine, reddish-orange metallic powder, usually an oxide.</term>, calcines it / and colors a person's hand black / and has within it a **degree of perfection** <note>original: "gradum perfectionis"</note>.

# The V. Chapter.
## The second Water by means of **Sal Ammoniac** <note>original: "Salmiax"</note>.

Take 1 pound of this described **Water** <note>represented by the symbol 🜔</note> and dissolve in it 4 **Loth** <term>Loth: A historical Germanic unit of weight, approximately 1/32 of a pound or about 15 grams.</term> of **Sal Ammoniac** <note>Ammonium chloride, a salt used in alchemy to make solvents more aggressive, specifically to dissolve gold.</note>, which should be pure and clear. When it has dissolved therein, the water will immediately take on a different form. For previously it was green and dissolved **Silver** <note>original: "☾"</note>, but not **Gold** <note>original: "☉"</note>. But immediately after the introduction of the Sal Ammoniac, it is turned to red, and it dissolves **Gold** into its **Mercury and Sulfur** <note>In alchemy, metals were believed to be composed of these two philosophical principles.</note>. And this is the second Water for the **dissolution of Gold** <note>original: "Soluirung ☉is"</note>, and not for silver; it stains a person’s hand red and keeps the color well, for with this we come to the second **Degree of Perfection** <note>original: "Grad Perfectionis"</note>.

# The VI. Chapter.
## The Water **OF THE PHILOSOPHERS** <note>original: "PHILOSOPHORVM"</note>.

Take 1 pound of the described **Water** and 12 **Loth** of the first **Mercury and Sulfur** <note>original: "☿ii 🜍ti"</note>; cast these all one after another into this Water. Seal the glass well so that the **virtue** <note>The "virtue" or "potency" refers to the volatile chemical power of the substance.</note> of the Sal Ammoniac does not smell or escape. Place it in warm ashes; the Water will then soon begin to attack and dissolve the **Mercury**. Let it stand in the heat until the Mercury is dissolved. And note: if the Water cannot entirely dissolve the Mercury in this way, then take out what is not dissolved, let it become dry with a gentle fire, and rub it with a new Water so that it dissolves. Do this as often as necessary until the Mercury is entirely dissolved into a water. Thereafter, put all these dissolved parts together in a well-closed glass and keep it diligently. This is the third **Water of the Philosophers**, and it possesses within it the third **Degree of Perfection**. The signs of this Water are: when copper plates are moistened in it, they become white, and it is a very heavy Water. This is a **Mother of the Living Water** <note>A foundational solvent capable of reducing metals to their liquid state.</note>, which leads and dissolves all **bodies** <note>original: "Leicknam," literally "corpses"; alchemists referred to solid metals as "dead" bodies that needed to be "resurrected" into a liquid state.</note> into their **First Matter**.

# The VIII. Chapter.
## How one should prepare the bodies when one wishes to transform them
## into their Prime Matter, etc.

Take a mark <note>A historical unit of weight, usually about 230 grams.</note> of pure gold <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note>, finely filed and cleanly rubbed on a stone with common salt. Dissolve the salt away with hot water and let the **gold calx** <term>Calx: The powdery residue left after a metal has been roasted or chemically broken down; an oxide.</term> settle to the bottom; pour the water off. Then, soak the calx three times with **Oil of Tartar** <term>Oil of Tartar: A concentrated, caustic solution of potassium carbonate, prized for its ability to dissolve substances.</term>, always letting the oil dry back into the gold calx. Afterward, put the calx into a glass and pour Oil of Tartar two fingers high over it so that it is well covered. Seal the glass at the top and let it stand in **horse manure** <term>Horse manure: A common alchemical heat source; the natural fermentation of the dung provided a steady, gentle warmth over many days.</term> for eight days so that it may putrefy. Then, remove the oil and dry the calx. Put it into the aforementioned living water over a gentle heat, and the calx will subtly transform into **liquid gold** <note>original: "☉ io", referring to the "Mercury of Gold"</note>. Let it stand until it is completely converted into liquid gold.

Afterward, gently pour off the water and put the **Mercury of the Body** <note>original: "Mercurium Corporis"</note> into a glass. Cleanse it with salt and vinegar, dry it, and squeeze it through a piece of fustian <note>original: "Parchet", a thick, durable cloth used as a fine filter.</note>. If it passes through completely, that is good; but if some of the gold calx remains that was not entirely dissolved, put it back into the **blessed water** so that it may be fully transformed into Mercury, without any error. This is the Mercury extracted from the body, which is now called **Corporal Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius Corporalis"</note>. It is not common mercury, but rather the **Mercury of the Philosophers**. The signs of this Mercury are that it is slow in its movement and not like the common sort, for it leaves its permanent earth behind it in the fire.

## Chapter VIII.
### How the bodies should be prepared when one wishes to transform them into their First Matter, etc.

Take one mark <term>Mark: A traditional European unit of weight for precious metals, roughly equal to 230 grams.</term> of fine, pure gold <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, finely filed and rubbed clean on a stone with common salt. Dissolve the salt away from it with hot water and let the gold-calx <note>A powder or "ash" produced by heating or chemically treating a metal.</note> settle to the bottom; pour the water off. Then saturate the calx three times with Oil of Tartar <note>original: *Oleo tartari*; a concentrated solution of potassium carbonate.</note>, always letting the oil dry back into the gold-calx. Afterward, put the calx into a glass and pour Oil of Tartar over it to a height of two fingers so that it is well covered. Seal the top of the glass and let it stand in horse manure <note>original: *Roßmist*; used by alchemists as a natural, steady source of gentle heat through fermentation.</note> for 8 days so that it may putrefy. Then remove the oil and dry the calx. Put it into the aforementioned living water over a gentle heat, and the calx will subtly transform into the mercury of gold <note>original: ☉ ☿</note>. Let it stand until it is completely converted into the mercury of gold. 

Afterward, gently pour off the water and put the Mercury of the Body <note>original: *Mercurium Corporis*</note> into a glass and clean it with salt and vinegar. Dry it and strain it through a fustian cloth <note>original: *Parchet*; a sturdy cloth used here as a filter.</note>. If it passes through entirely, that is good; however, if any of the gold-calx remains that was not fully dissolved, put it back into the "Blessed Water" so that it may be completely transformed into mercury without any error. This is the mercury extracted from the body, which is now called Corporal Mercury <note>original: *Mercurius Corporalis*</note>. It is not common mercury, but rather the Mercury of the Philosophers <note>original: *Mercurius Philosophorum*</note>. The signs of this mercury are that it is slow in its movement and not like common mercury, for it leaves its "permanent earth" behind it in the fire.

# The IX. Chapter.
->The English Practice Follows.<-

Now begins the meaning and the way of the **Elixir of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Elixir Philosophorum"</note>, both white and red, made solely from the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Mercurio Philosophorum"</note>, from Mercury, and all the minerals of the bodies <note>In alchemy, "bodies" (Leichnam) refers to the solid metals.</note>, so that they may withstand the test, made from the <term>Antimony <note>represented by the symbol ♁io</note></term> of the Wise, which is not the common kind. This is what the philosophers call the **Prime Matter** <note>original: "erste Materi"</note>: it is a watery element, cold and moist, the eternally constant water, the spirit out of the body, the sweet-smelling **Oil of Violets**, the blessed water, the Water of the Wise, the water of the PHILOSOPHERS, the flower of eternal grace, the **Virgin’s Milk**, and many other names it has in the books of the philosophers that are written to be unintelligible. All these names mean only one thing: that is our **Mercury of the Wise**. From this alone comes the **Alchemical Virtue** <note>original: "Virtus Alchy"</note> and the **white and red tincture**. Geber, the philosopher, says: Our art is not found through superfluous goods. For there is only one stone, one art, and one medicine, in which the entire mastery is hidden; we should add nothing foreign to it, but rather, in its preparation, remove the excess. For in it, and through it, are all things that belong to it. We should not add foreign goods by way of <term>Gold <note>represented by the symbol ☉</note></term> and <term>Silver <note>represented by the symbol ☽</note></term>, for they are not foreign, but are helpful at the very end as a source, a leaven, or a ferment, so that the work may be completed. For another philosopher, Diomedes, says: You seekers, do not take any foreign powder for the stone against the laws of nature. For our Elixir is, and shall be, only drawn out of the **Mercury of the Wise**, and all other things are nothing but salt, alum, vitriol, and strong waters, etc. The aforementioned **Antimony** <note>represented by the symbol ♁ius</note>, however, is a tall tree with countless branches and a root of the philosophers, from which much fruit comes. And the stone is recognized in the books of the philosophers who possessed it.

### To turn the white sulfur into red.

## Turning the White Sulfur into Red.
